facts.text: A technology readiness level (TRL) is a maturity score from 1 to 9, ranging from a basic idea at TRL 1 to a system proven in real operation at TRL 9; ISO 16290:2013 defines TRLs for space systems.
facts.quote: A technology readiness level is a 1 to 9 score of how mature a technology is, from a basic idea (TRL 1) to a system proven in real operation (TRL 9), defined for space systems in ISO 16290:2013.

facts.text: Technology readiness levels began at NASA in the 1990s as a shared vocabulary for program reviews.
facts.quote: TRLs began at NASA in the 1990s as a shared vocabulary for program reviews.

facts.text: ISO 16290:2013 standardizes technology readiness levels and their assessment criteria.
facts.quote: ISO 16290:2013 standardizes the levels and their assessment criteria [Chapter 12].

facts.text: Mining uses technology readiness level vocabulary for collision systems.
facts.quote: Mining uses the vocabulary for collision systems.

facts.text: The South African MOSH test specification requires independent verification at TRL 4 and TRL 7 stage gates for collision systems.
facts.quote: The South African MOSH test specification requires independent verification at TRL 4 and TRL 7 stage gates

facts.text: At TRL 9, the South African MOSH test specification calls for statistical monitoring of collision systems in production, for example over three months or 2,000 hours.
facts.quote: at TRL 9 calls for statistical monitoring in production, for example over three months or 2,000 hours.

facts.text: The University of Pretoria runs a staged protocol for collision systems from laboratory-scale TRL 4 tests to mine-like trials.
facts.quote: The University of Pretoria runs a staged protocol from laboratory-scale TRL 4 tests to mine-like trials [Chapters 3, 7, 8].

facts.text: The booklet concludes that technology readiness levels are useful vocabulary but weak measurement: a component can be mature while integration, data, model credibility, scenario coverage and the safety argument are not.
facts.quote: because a component can be mature while integration, data, model credibility, scenario coverage and the safety argument are not.

facts.text: Practitioners reported 15 challenges with technology readiness levels, with the most critical challenges at system and integration level.
facts.quote: Practitioners reported 15 challenges, the most critical at system and integration level

facts.text: The booklet recommends assigning technology readiness levels only to genuinely novel elements, never assigning one average TRL to the whole program.
facts.quote: Assign TRLs only to genuinely novel elements, never one average for the whole program

facts.text: The booklet recommends using a simulation credibility scale such as NASA-STD-7009B for the toolchain.
facts.quote: use a simulation credibility scale such as NASA-STD-7009B for the toolchain [Chapter 12].

facts.text: A high TRL for a sensor or brake controller says nothing about the credibility of the simulator testing them; technology readiness and simulation credibility measure different things, and the program needs both scales.
facts.quote: A high TRL for the sensor or brake controller says nothing about whether the simulator that tests them is credible; the two scales measure different things and the program needs both [Chapter 12].
